description: scripts/usdc-balance.py prints its result with Python's bare `print(int(r["result"], 16) / 10**6)`. For a very small non-zero balance (e.g. exactly 1 raw unit = 0.000001 USDC) Python renders this in scientific notation ('1e-06'); for a sufficiently large balance it could similarly switch to exponential form. Every current call site in run.sh double-quotes the captured value before use, so no literal shell word-splitting bug was found, but there is no test (unit or fixture) proving that a scientific-notation string round-trips correctly through `Number(process.argv[...])` in the decideSpawn/buildSeedPlan node -e invocations, nor through jq/bash arithmetic contexts, before real money is at stake.
